questions.stem: According to Article 74 of the Indian Constitution, who strictly heads the Union Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President?
questions.explanation: Article 74(1) states: 'There shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President who shall, in the exercise of his functions, act in accordance with such advice.'

questions.stem: Under the parliamentary system established by the Indian Constitution, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to which specific constitutional body?

options.option_text: The Lok Sabha (House of the People)
The Supreme Court of India (alternative interpretation)

questions.explanation: Article 75(3) explicitly states that the Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the House of the People (Lok Sabha). This is the bedrock principle of India's parliamentary democracy: if a government loses the majority in the Lok Sabha, all ministers must resign.

questions.stem: According to the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act (2003), the total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Council of Ministers shall NOT exceed what percentage of the total strength of the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: The 91st Amendment Act capped the size of the Union Council of Ministers at 15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha. This was done to prevent jumbo cabinets and reduce political defection/bribery through ministerial posts.

questions.stem: Who officially administers the constitutionally mandated oaths of office and secrecy to the Union Ministers before they legally enter upon their office?

options.option_text: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: Article 75(4) states that before a Minister enters upon his office, the President shall administer to him the oaths of office and of secrecy according to the forms set out for the purpose in the Third Schedule.

questions.stem: While the Council is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, the principle of 'individual responsibility' means that a Union Minister strictly holds office during the pleasure of the:
questions.explanation: Article 75(2) states that the Ministers shall hold office during the pleasure of the President. In practice, the President exercises this pleasure ONLY on the advice of the Prime Minister, meaning the PM can ask a minister to resign at any time.

The Cabinet is a smaller, core decision-making group of senior ministers, whereas the Council of Ministers is the larger body comprising all categories of ministers.

questions.explanation: The Council of Ministers (COM) is the constitutional body comprising 60 to 80 ministers of three categories: Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers. The 'Cabinet' is a smaller inner circle of 15 to 20 senior ministers who hold key portfolios (Home, Defence, Finance) and take all major policy decisions.
